title: sovereign debt / investor composition / non bank investors | Research Paper | Who holds sovereign debt and why it matters
summary: BIS Working Paper No. 1099 constructs a dataset of sovereign debt holdings by investor type (bank, non-bank private, official) for 95 countries over 20 years, finding that private non-bank investors (mainly investment funds) fund nearly 70% of increases in sovereign debt and are most responsive to yield changes. For emerging markets, a 10% debt increase leads to 6.7% cost increase normally, but 9% if non-bank investors are absent, indicating sovereigns are structurally vulnerable to losing non-bank participation.
